sidebar.keyIdeasHint: Keep these four ideas in view.

page1.idea1: Processed context is used for prediction.

page2.idea3: Most likely picks the highest chance.
page2.idea4: The chosen Token joins the text.

page3.idea1: The model predicts one Token at a time.
page3.idea2: Many Tokens can have a chance, not just one.
page3.idea3: The chances change when the context changes.
page3.idea4: A selected Token is added to the text, then the model predicts again.

page4.idea4: Use the new text and repeat.

page1.title: What happens next?
page1.subtitle: From processed context to the next-Token prediction.
page1.bridgeLine1: In Lesson 3, the model combined information from the available token positions to build a richer representation of the current text.
page1.bridgeLine2: Now it can use that processed information to:
page1.bridgeEmphasis: predict what token might come next.
page1.processedCopy: Information from the available token positions has been combined into a richer representation of the current text.
page1.whatNextCopy: The model uses this processed information to estimate which token might come next.
page1.technical: The model’s estimate of what token might come next, based on the information available so far.
page1.keyIdea1: Large Language Models generate text one token at a time.
page1.keyIdea2: They repeatedly predict the next token, add it to the context, and predict again.
page1.thinkCopy: If several tokens could come next, how can the model compare the possibilities?
page1.thinkNext: Let’s find out on the next page.

scorePage.title: How does the model compare what could come next?
scorePage.subtitle: See how possible next Tokens receive different internal scores.
scorePage.intro1: The model considers many Tokens that could follow.
scorePage.intro2Before: It gives each possibility an internal
scorePage.intro2After: based on the information it has processed.
scorePage.technical: An internal number the model uses to compare possible next Tokens.
scorePage.sourceTitle: Where do the scores come from?
scorePage.sourceCopy: The model uses the information it has processed and patterns it learned during training.
scorePage.sourceCompare: Together, these help it calculate a score for each possible next Token.
scorePage.noCalculation: The exact calculation happens inside the model—you do not calculate it yourself.
scorePage.higherMeans: A higher score means the model currently favours that Token more.
scorePage.notProbability: A score is not a probability yet.
scorePage.illustrative: Illustrative comparison only — these are not real model values.

page2.title: How does the model choose one Token?
page2.subtitle: Keep the whole distribution visible while one selection rule chooses and adds a Token.
page2.technical: Greedy decoding always chooses the highest-probability Token. Sampling makes a chance-based choice from the whole distribution, so higher-probability Tokens are more likely but not guaranteed.
page2.greedyExplanation: Most likely mode selected the Token with the highest probability.
page2.samplingExplanation: Chance-based mode sampled from all four probabilities; a lower-probability Token can sometimes be selected.
page2.updatedContext: Updated text — now the next context
page2.predictAgain: The new empty position starts another prediction.
page2.takeaway: The model compares many Token probabilities, chooses one Token using a selection rule, adds it to the text, then predicts again.

page3.title: Watch the Model Predict
page3.subtitle: Watch a real language model continue text one Token at a time.

page4.title: Check what you discovered
page4.subtitle: Explain the most important step in the generation loop.
page4.heading: What happens after a Token is added?
page4.intro: Choose the answer that describes real next-Token generation.
page4.afterAdded: After one Token is added, what happens next?
page4.answerPlanned: The model already knows the rest of the sentence.
page4.answerContext: The updated text becomes the new context, and the model predicts another Token.
page4.guidance: Look back at the live text: each new Token changes the context for the next prediction.
page4.discovery: Exactly. The updated text becomes the new context, so the model predicts another Token.

live.title: Watch a real model predict
live.intro: Start with a short text, then watch the model predict, add and repeat automatically.
live.modelBoundary: Every prediction on this page comes from a small language model running on our server.
live.temperatureTechnical: Temperature changes how spread out the next-Token probabilities are. Lower values make the strongest options stand out more. Higher values spread the probability across more options. It does not change what the model has learned.
live.errorTitle: The live model could not run
live.errorHelp: Your text and completed lesson progress are safe. Try the request again, or continue with Back and Next.

page5.title: Predict, add and repeat
page5.subtitle: A longer sentence grows through several one-Token prediction cycles.
page5.question: How can one-Token prediction create longer text?
page5.intro: Use a reviewed starter. Compare the visible candidate chances, select one piece, place it, then repeat with a new candidate set.
page5.discovery: Each selected Token changes the text, so the next set of candidate chances can also change.
page5.takeaway: A language model generates text by predicting, adding and repeating one Token at a time.
page5.boundary: Simplified local candidate tree. This is not full Qwen generation and no model weights are loaded.
page5.bridge: Put the complete one-Token-at-a-time journey together.

page6.title: Lesson summary
page6.subtitle: The model compares possible next tokens, turns scores into probabilities, and generates text one token at a time.
page6.idea1Copy: The model considers many possible continuations.
page6.idea2Copy: Possible tokens receive different internal scores.
page6.idea3Copy: Scores are turned into a probability distribution.
page6.idea4Copy: One token is selected, added to the context, and the process repeats.
page6.recap: The model generates text by comparing possibilities and predicting one token at a time.
page6.nuance: A higher probability does not guarantee a token will always be selected.
page6.next: Now that you’ve seen how predictions are made, Lesson 5 explains where those learned patterns came from.

probabilityPage.title: From scores to probabilities
probabilityPage.subtitle: Turn internal scores into easier-to-compare probabilities.
probabilityPage.intro1: Scores are useful inside the model, but they are hard for us to compare.
probabilityPage.intro2After: so we can see how likely each option is.
probabilityPage.technical: A number that shows how likely one possible next Token is compared with the other possibilities.
probabilityPage.guaranteeTitle: Higher probability = more likely, not guaranteed
probabilityPage.guaranteeLine1: A Token with a higher probability is more likely to be chosen next.
probabilityPage.guaranteeLine2: But it is not always guaranteed — there are different ways a model can choose from the possible next Tokens.
probabilityPage.guaranteeLine3: We’ll explore one factor that can affect this choice later.
probabilityPage.illustrative: Illustrative example — not real model output.
probabilityPage.whyCopy1: Probabilities are easier to understand and compare than internal scores.
probabilityPage.whyCopy2: They help us see which options are more likely right now.
probabilityPage.whyRemember: Remember: more likely does not mean definitely chosen.

quiz.title: Check the idea
quiz.subtitle: Review the key ideas about predicting the next token.
quiz.quickQuestions: 4 quick questions to see what you remember.
quiz.answerEach: Answer each question, then check your answer.
quiz.completionText: You can now explain how a model compares next-token choices and continues generating text.
quiz.completedIdea3: A chosen token updates the context
quiz.completedIdea4: Temperature can change how varied choices are
quiz.q1Prompt: The model gives several possible next tokens different scores. What does a higher score mean?
quiz.q1A: The token will definitely be chosen
quiz.q1B: The model currently considers the token a better fit for the context
quiz.q1C: The token appeared more times in the sentence
quiz.q1Correct: A higher score means the model currently considers that token a better fit based on the processed context and patterns learned during training.
quiz.q1Incorrect: The score is used to compare possible next tokens. A higher score does not guarantee that the token will be chosen.
quiz.q2Prompt: A possible next token has a probability of 46%. What does this mean?
quiz.q2A: The token will definitely be chosen
quiz.q2C: This token is more likely to be chosen than options with lower probabilities
quiz.q2D: 46% of the sentence contains this token
quiz.q2Correct: Probability tells us how likely one possible next token is compared with the other possibilities. Higher probability means more likely — not guaranteed.
quiz.q2Incorrect: Probability is about how likely a possible next token is compared with the other options. It does not mean the token is guaranteed to be chosen.
quiz.q3Prompt: The model chooses one next token. What happens next?
quiz.q3A: The whole sentence is finished immediately
quiz.q3B: The token is added to the context, and the model predicts again
quiz.q3C: The model deletes the previous tokens
quiz.q3D: The probabilities stay exactly the same
quiz.q3Correct: The chosen token becomes part of the context. The model then uses the updated context to predict another token. This is how an LLM can generate text one token at a time.
quiz.q3Incorrect: Remember that generation is a repeated process: choose a token, add it to the context, then predict again.
quiz.q4Prompt: In the interactive model, what did changing the temperature affect?
quiz.q4A: How many tokens fit inside the context window
quiz.q4B: How the text is split into tokens
quiz.q4C: How focused or varied the model's next-token choices can be
quiz.q4D: How many training examples the model has seen
quiz.q4Correct: Lower temperature tends to make the model's choices more focused and predictable. Higher temperature can make the output more varied.
quiz.q4Incorrect: Temperature affects the model's next-token choices. It does not change tokenisation, context-window size, or the model's training data.
